findings.detail: M3 core defect (root cause): v3_cycle.run_discovery_cycle scores candidates via ScoringService, which promotes candidates.status to 'ELIGIBLE'; the subsequent ExecutiveDecisionService.evaluate() query eligible_candidates() (executive/eligibility.py line ~367) only considers status IN ('NEW','SCORED'), so every freshly-scored V3 candidate is invisible to selection. Every flag-ON cycle therefore terminates WAITING/'NO_ELIGIBLE_CANDIDATES'. Proven two ways: (1) pytest instrumentation captured all 6 in-suite cycles as WAITING including 'v3-lab-1' and dual-path 'dual-on'; (2) standalone drive shows assess_eligibility()=eligible while eligible_candidates()=0. The select→compile_mission→mission.created path is unreachable code as shipped.

M3's PASS rests on a vacuous assertion: test_flag_on_lab_loop_observe_to_mission guards ALL mission.created checks behind 'if report.outcome == "COMPILED":' and accepts WAITING; test_worker_loop_dual_path_flag_on_compiles likewise only asserts a cycle_completed event exists. Since COMPILED never occurs (finding 1), these tests pass while asserting nothing about discovery-to-mission. The handoff §9 criterion 'One discovery-to-mission loop (flag ON, lab)' is NOT met; the gate report's M3 PASS is unsupported by its cited evidence.

Second independent blocker: even when candidate visibility is repaired (reviewer scratch experiment demoting ELIGIBLE→SCORED so eligible_candidates() sees it), the legacy executive ranker scores the standard lab fixture candidate 0.070 against min_action_score 0.40 ('waiting beats acting'). Fixing only the SQL filter would still yield zero compiled missions; the threshold/ranking interplay between the new policy-based portfolio and the legacy action scorer was never integrated or tested end-to-end.

Gate report evidence lines misstate test counts: M1 claims 8/8 (junit: 9 tests), M2 claims 14/14 (junit: 13), M5 claims 5/5 (junit: 4). The underlying suites do pass, but the gate report's numbers do not match the very artifacts it cites, indicating it was not generated from them.

test_v3_smoke restart-window assertion 'assert len(second_missions) <= max(1, count_after_first)' permits mission-count growth and, given the compile defect, never observes a mission at all — the crash-window resume-once property is unproven at mission level. STOP-before-work, exactly-once cycle records per loop_id, EventConflict-on-rewrite, and rebuild-zero-drift ARE substantively tested and pass.

notes: Independent re-execution confirms M1 (9/9 incl. rebuild zero-drift and v34→v35 in-place migration), M2 (13/13 plus my own two-DB determinism probe: traces identical modulo random ids), M6 (7/7 disposable remote, ls-remote truth, no blind retry), M7 (8/8 PASSED-only/distinct/honest-UNKNOWN), and M8 (baseline 1459→phase4 1522, monotonic, zero failures across all six junit XMLs; delta JSONs match the XMLs). Flag governance is sound: discovery.cycle_enabled defaults false everywhere, wired only at the worker_loop choke point, nothing forces it true, the v3_loop WAIT+ExecutiveDecisionService fallback survives the observe_for_cycle extraction intact (diff reviewed, test_v3_loop green), no production wiring was touched (production checkout lacks b913c75 entirely), and boundary probes confirm fail-closed BLOCKED without a registered policy and STOP blocking before observation with the observer provably never invoked. However, M3 FAILS at substance: instrumenting pytest proves the unified cycle NEVER compiles a mission in any test — ScoringService's ELIGIBLE status makes candidates invisible to the executive's NEW/SCORED query, and even with visibility forced, the legacy ranker scores the fixture candidate below threshold — so 'one discovery-to-mission loop (flag ON, lab)' does not exist, hidden behind conditional assertions that pass vacuously. Per verdict rules this is an overall FAIL; repair must make the flagged path actually reach mission.created with an unconditional assertion, then re-run M3/M5 and regenerate the gate report with corrected counts.
